verdict.rationale: Warp documents an Automation Platform whose cloud agents are explicitly "autonomous, background agents". They can be started by system events, recurring schedules, custom webhooks, or integrations such as Slack and GitHub. API keys support headless operation, and each run produces an inspectable transcript. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that scheduled and triggered background automations work reliably in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Cloud agents are autonomous, background agents that run on Warp’s cloud infrastructure or your own, triggered by system events, schedules, or integrations like Slack and GitHub.
The Automation Platform runs cloud agents from triggers, schedules, integrations, and APIs. Use it for background work such as issue triage, pull request review
Schedules: Run recurring tasks like dependency updates or dead code removal
Triggers: React to events from Slack, Linear, GitHub, or custom webhooks
API keys let the Oz CLI, cloud agents, and self-hosted workers authenticate without human interaction.
